title: Lemon Marmalade
subtitle: Sharp, clear, intensely lemony preserve
excerpt: Lemon marmalade is sharper and more intense than orange, with a jewel-yellow colour. The whole lemon goes in, peel, juice, and pips in muslin for pectin. Makes about four 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Lemons have very high pectin in the pips and pith, squeezed muslin is essential.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and soak the peel the evening before.

glossaryTerms.definition: 105 °C for marmalade. Confirmed by the wrinkle test on a chilled plate.

content.text: Lemon marmalade has a sharper, more acidic character than orange marmalade and a clear, bright yellow colour. It sets firmly,  lemon pips have enormous amounts of pectin. Good on toast, excellent with smoked salmon, and useful in baking wherever lemon flavour is wanted in a spreadable form. Makes about four 450 g jars.

Scrub and halve the lemons. Juice them and reserve the juice. Scrape all the pips and pith into a muslin square and tie tightly. Shred the peel into thin strips,  thin-cut works better than thick for lemon, as the peel is more pithy and thick shreds can be chewy. Put the peel, muslin bundle, juice, and water into the jam pan.
Simmer until the peel is soft

Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 1 to 1½ hours until the peel is completely soft. Press a shred between your fingers,  it should collapse. Lemon peel takes longer than orange peel to soften fully.
Lift out the muslin bundle and squeeze hard. Add the sugar and stir over low heat until fully dissolved. Raise to a full rolling boil and cook until 105 (the
) °C, about 10 to 15 minutes. Test on a cold plate. Skim, rest 10 minutes, stir gently, then ladle into hot sterilised jars and seal.

items.symptom: Peel is still tough in the jar
items.cause: Not softened enough before sugar was added.
items.fix: Simmer for the full 1½ hours, or overnight. Once sugar is in, the peel stops softening.

items.cause: High lemon acidity concentrated during the boil.
items.fix: Reduce lemon quantity to 800 g and supplement with 200 g of orange next time, or reduce the boiling time slightly.

items.symptom: Peel turns translucent and disappears into the jar
items.fix: Cut a touch thicker or reduce the boiling time by 2 to 3 minutes.

items.cause: Undissolved sugar, or the boil went slightly past setting point and concentrated the sugar too much.
items.fix: Always stir until sugar is clear before raising heat. Gently warm crystallised jars in a bowl of hot water.
